title: Perfect representatives weakly generate
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with chosen derived localizations of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and of the modules on every open, in one Hom universe. Give $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] its inherited triangulated structure. Suppose its perfect localizing closure [def-pc-perfect-localizing-closure] is the whole category. Let $(P_i)_{i\in I}$ be a family indexed by a set in the scheme universe, such that every perfect object [def-pc-perfect-complex] is isomorphic to some $P_i$. With the coproducts provided by lem-pc-derived-qcoh-direct-sums, this family is generating [def-pc-generators]: its coproduct is a weak generator. Compactness of the $P_i$ is not assumed.

source.place: Tag 09IS; orthogonal-class reduction in lem-pc-derived-qcoh-compact-generation, proof step 2

proof.text: Use the supplied coproducts. If every map from the coproduct into every shift of K is zero, extend a map on an individual summand using zero maps on the other summands. The representative isomorphisms give the same vanishing for every perfect object. Shift adjunction converts target-shift vanishing to source-shift vanishing.

The class of objects A for which every map A[m] to K is zero is isomorphism-invariant, shift-closed, retract-closed, and sum-closed by the coproduct universal property and preservation of sums by shifts. For a cone, exactness of Hom makes its map to K factor through the shift of the first triangle term, so it vanishes. This class contains every perfect object and hence contains their localizing closure. The supplied equality with top puts K in it. Its identity is zero, so K is zero, including the empty-family case.

mathlib_searches.query: Perfect representatives whose localizing closure is the whole derived category have a coproduct which is a weak generator
A set of representatives of objects generating a localizing subcategory has coproduct a weak generator of the triangulated category

from.place: proof, first step: compare the dualizing sheaves of the source and target under the finite morphism; orthogonal-class argument in compact generation
